public_and_capability_observations.observation: A Git tree can encode multiple path additions/deletions relative to a base tree; publishing requires creating a commit and then updating a branch ref.
GitHub exposes creation of a commit from a tree SHA and explicit parent commit SHA.
Update-reference with force=false enforces a fast-forward update and can return conflict; the ref is the publication boundary after tree/commit creation.

This invocation exposes create_tree, create_commit and update_ref(force=false), so the candidate publication primitive is Chat-exposed rather than an unavailable external executor. The destructive GC path was not executed against primary/protected state.

model.scope: Repository-local retained checkpoint whose complete recovery-root membership, sweeper epoch, and target incarnation are represented in the same branch/tree publication domain. Complete repository rollback or roots outside that domain are excluded from the positive claim and remain unresolved.

root_flip_after_final_check.definition: marked dead, final check sees unrooted/current epoch/same target, then target becomes a live recovery root before deletion
root_flip_after_final_check.single_ref_commit_fenced: 0/6 live-root deletion; 6/6 publication conflict/fail-closed because root change advances the same ref domain

same_path_reincarnation_after_mark.definition: marked dead/currently unrooted, path is recreated before effect
same_path_reincarnation_after_mark.single_ref_commit_fenced: 0/6 wrong-incarnation deletion via ref publication conflict

unrelated_head_advance.definition: target remains dead/same incarnation/current epoch but another branch-head change occurs before publish
unrelated_head_advance.single_ref_commit_fenced: 0/3 delete; 3/3 false blockage/leak until retry on the newer head

applied_response_lost_happy_path.definition: all strong guards pass, publication applies, response is lost
applied_response_lost_happy_path.recheck_then_contents_delete_sha: correct deletion but 1 duplicate delete attempt on blind retry
applied_response_lost_happy_path.single_ref_commit_fenced: correct deletion, 0 duplicate delete attempts by ref/transition readback reconciliation

scope_safe_conclusion.negative: A per-file current-SHA delete fences target reincarnation but does not atomically fence a concurrent change to the recovery-root manifest; root recheck then Contents delete has a TOCTOU gap.
scope_safe_conclusion.candidate: When all recovery-root membership and target identity are in one repository ref authority domain, build one tree/commit that both removes the exact retained target and advances the GC/root manifest, with the pinned current commit as parent; publish only via update_ref(force=false). Any intervening root-set change, target reincarnation, or unrelated head advance makes the proposal non-fast-forward and must fail closed/recompute. Persist an applied_transition_id in the resulting manifest/tree so ambiguous response is reconciled by current-ref/tree readback before retry.
scope_safe_conclusion.tradeoff: The single-ref commit is safety-strong but conservative: unrelated head advances produce false blockage/leak until a retry rebuilds from the new head. In this lattice it leaked 45 dead copies versus 42 for recheck+per-file delete, while eliminating the latter's 6 live-root deletions.
not_proven: No claim for recovery roots stored outside the same ref/tree authority domain.
No claim against complete repository rollback/restore that erases every current manifest and transition witness.
No destructive GC execution against protected/primary authority was performed; this is a finite model plus documented/exposed primitive audit.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.chat_exposed_primitive: GitHub create_tree/create_commit/update_ref plus readback; repository rate-limit interruption remains fail-closed

frontier: GC throughput / hotspot leaf: batch multiple dead retained copies into one tree/commit and compare whole-root CAS contention against sharded retention manifests without reintroducing cross-domain root/delete races.
Complete repository rollback with loss of every transition witness remains unresolved and must not be papered over with paid/protected external coordination.
exact_continuation: Model batched and sharded GC publication. Compare one global retention-root commit, prefix-sharded manifests with per-shard ref or path roots, deterministic batch IDs, and no-delete fallback. Adversaries: two sweepers selecting overlapping dead sets, concurrent LATEST/root promotion across shards, batch response loss, one shard rate-limited, target reincarnation, and unrelated head churn. Measure live-root deletion, duplicate batch/delete effects, dead-copy leakage, false conflicts/hotspot pressure, and recovery reads. Positive claims require root membership and deletion publication to share an atomic authority domain; otherwise retain/fail closed.
